Individual-level cross-validation folds shared across traits and models

Source: R/cv_folds.R
cv_folds.Rd

cv_folds() assigns every individual (not every row) to one of v folds, separately within each group (e.g. herd) and independently in each repeat. The resulting fold table is meant to be created once and then reused with apply_folds() for every trait, trait pair and model, so that all compared models are validated on exactly the same individuals.

Repeats are generated one after another (repeat 1 for all groups, then repeat 2, ...), so with the same seed the first repeats do not change when repeats is increased later.

cv_folds(
  data,
  id,
  by = NULL,
  v = 5L,
  repeats = 1L,
  strata = NULL,
  breaks = 4L,
  pool = 0.1,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or data.table with one or more records per individual.

id

Individual ID column (name or index). All records of an individual always fall into the same fold.

by

Optional grouping column(s); folds are built within each group. An individual must belong to exactly one group.

v

Number of folds (>= 2).

repeats

Number of repeats (>= 1).

strata

Optional column to stratify on (must be constant within an individual). Numeric columns are binned into breaks quantile bins and strata smaller than pool are merged, as in split_cv().

breaks, pool

See split_cv().

seed

Optional seed; the global random number stream is left untouched.

Value

A data.table with one row per individual and repeat: the by column(s), the id column, rep ("Repeat01", ...) and fold ("Fold1", ...): the fold in which the individual is validated.

See also

apply_folds(), cv_scenarios()

Examples

dat <- data.frame(id = paste0("i", 1:40), herd = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 20),
                  adg = rnorm(40), bf = rnorm(40))
folds <- cv_folds(dat, id = "id", by = "herd", v = 5, repeats = 2, seed = 1)
folds[, .N, by = .(herd, rep, fold)]
#>       herd     rep   fold     N
#>     <char>  <char> <char> <int>
#>  1:      A Repeat1  Fold4     4
#>  2:      A Repeat1  Fold2     4
#>  3:      A Repeat1  Fold1     4
#>  4:      A Repeat1  Fold3     4
#>  5:      A Repeat1  Fold5     4
#>  6:      B Repeat1  Fold5     4
#>  7:      B Repeat1  Fold4     4
#>  8:      B Repeat1  Fold2     4
#>  9:      B Repeat1  Fold1     4
#> 10:      B Repeat1  Fold3     4
#> 11:      A Repeat2  Fold1     4
#> 12:      A Repeat2  Fold3     4
#> 13:      A Repeat2  Fold2     4
#> 14:      A Repeat2  Fold5     4
#> 15:      A Repeat2  Fold4     4
#> 16:      B Repeat2  Fold2     4
#> 17:      B Repeat2  Fold1     4
#> 18:      B Repeat2  Fold3     4
#> 19:      B Repeat2  Fold4     4
#> 20:      B Repeat2  Fold5     4
#>       herd     rep   fold     N
#>     <char>  <char> <char> <int>
